Time from spawn to the first frame was measured in a PTY at 100x30, 15 runs per cell, median with min and max. With the launcher as shipped, the Counter takes 1101 ms (range 1009-1280) and the Dashboard 1233 ms (1158-1349). With `java` started directly, they take 1034 ms and 1125 ms. A plain jatatui program in Java, with no Scala and no Kyo, takes 147 ms and 56 MB. So the JVM plus crossterm costs about 150 ms. The other 850-950 ms is the tui4s, Kyo and Scala stack, and most of it is cold class loading.

Where the time goes (Counter, direct, median of 5 runs):
- JVM boot until the TuiApp constructor runs: 66 ms.
- The constructor (SchedulerDefaults and OutputCapture load about 230 Scala collection classes): 119 ms.
- Start of the Kyo runtime: 377 ms. This covers about 1,070 classes and many lambda bootstraps. It also includes a sleep loop of 86-102 ms in Kyo's BlockingMonitor, which probes the CPU-time resolution (ThreadUserTime.probeResolution). I called the probe directly: it returns 12.8 ms on this machine.
- Terminal enter: 110 ms. Loading the JNI library, which also copies the .so out of the jar, takes 25 ms. Linking the FFM isatty downcall takes 76 ms. Raw mode and the alternate screen take 9 ms.
- UI build, mount, settle, layout, paint and flush: about 245 ms. For the Dashboard this part is about 400 ms.

No class was loaded from kyo-http, kyo-net, kyo-ffi, kyo-schema, kyo-system, pprint, JMH, commons-math3, asm or jopt-simple. Together those jars are 12.7 MB of the 38 MB lib directory.

Running work concurrently helps, and the results are measured:
- A background thread that loads the JNI library and links isatty while Kyo starts saves 113 ms (Counter) and 77 ms (Dashboard).
- Setting `-Dkyo.scheduler.blockingMonitorMinIntervalNs=12800000` skips the probe. This is not concurrency; it removes the wait. It saves 100 ms and 69 ms.
- A class preloader thread with a list from a training run saves 306 ms and 319 ms.
- With all changes but no AOT cache, the first frame comes at 537 ms and 614 ms.

The JDK 25 AOT cache alone gives 521 ms and 588 ms, about half. Combined with the probe skip, the JNI and isatty preload, C1 and SerialGC, the first frame comes at 320 ms (Counter) and 395 ms (Dashboard). That is about 70% less than the shipped launcher, and RSS goes down to 93 MB and 134 MB, from 125 MB and 164 MB. Using only launcher flags, with no code change, gives 361 ms and 433 ms.

The cache is 37-40 MB per app. It still works when the install directory moves. A changed jar mtime makes it invalid. With `AOTMode=auto`, a stale or missing cache prints warnings into the terminal before the UI, unless the launcher adds `-Xlog:aot=off`.

## Method
- Machine: container with 4 vCPU and 16 GB. JDK 25.0.4.1 (Ubuntu build). Worktree `wt-perf` at origin/main cd6a877.
- The examples' only use of pini4s is a test, so I removed pini4s from the worktree build and deleted that test, as the earlier spike did (vendor/pini4s is a submodule that is not checked out, and reading other repositories is not allowed). Nothing was committed or pushed.
- PTY driver `perf/ptytime.py` (it uses a copy of examples/ptycheck/vt.py):
  - It opens a 100x30 PTY with TERM=xterm-256color, takes `t0 = time.monotonic_ns()`, then starts the process with the PTY as its controlling terminal.
  - It feeds all output into the VT emulator. "alt-screen" is the first `?1049h`. "frame" is the first time the alternate screen holds the full last line (`q quits`). The first visible text came at the same moment as the full frame in every run.
  - It waits 300 ms after the frame, reads VmHWM from /proc/PID/status, then sends `q`. `wait4` gives ru_maxrss.
  - It removes JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS from the environment (the container's proxy flags print "Picked up..." into the terminal) and sets JAVA_HOME to JDK 25 (the container's default is JDK 21).
- Clocks: Python's monotonic clock, Java's System.nanoTime and the `-Xlog` decorator `tn` all read CLOCK_MONOTONIC. So the PTY times, the app marks and the class-load lines share one time line.
- Matrix: `perf/bench.py`. 15 rounds, and each round runs every mode x app combination in a shuffled order. Page cache is warm; cold start was not measured. load1 during the runs: median 2.1 (the harness itself). The `launcher`, `direct` and `aot` modes ran in both batches, and their medians differ by at most 37 ms between batches.
- Anatomy:
  - A temporary build with timestamp marks: `PerfMark`, active only with `-Dtui4s.perf=<file>`.
  - `-Xlog:class+load` and `-Xlog:startuptime` (1 run per app, with class logging on).
  - Phase timings without class logging: median of 5 runs.
  - A stack sampler thread (1 run) to find the time gaps.
- Every temporary code change is in `perf/wt-perf-temporary.diff`.

## Concurrency (step 3)
Constraints of the experiment:
- The prewarm thread is a daemon platform thread that starts on the first line of the TuiApp constructor.
- It does not change the terminal. It writes nothing to stdout or stderr. It swallows its own errors.
- Raw mode, the alternate screen, the release bracket and the shutdown hook stay exactly where they are. So the restore guarantees do not change.

Entering the terminal early on another thread would show a blank alternate screen about 500 ms sooner, but the first frame would not come sooner. It would also need a second restore path that exists before the bracket. I do not recommend it.

What I measured, as median change against direct (counter / dashboard):
- JNI load + isatty link off the critical path (about 100 ms of work): -113 / -77.
- Probe skip (one property, the same probed value): -100 / -69.
- List-driven class preloader thread (`Class.forName(name, false)`), list taken from a training log up to the first frame: -306 / -319, including the native part.
- All code changes + C1 + SerialGC, no AOT: 537 / 614.
- What remains on the critical path is static initialization, the interpreter and lambda linkage.

## AOT cache (step 4)
- Training: one-step `-XX:AOTCacheOutput`, with a scripted PTY session (keys sent after the first frame). Exit after `q` takes about 2.5 s more while the JVM forks a child that builds the cache. Cache size: 37.6 MB (counter) and 40.6 MB (dashboard).
- Validated with `-XX:AOTMode=on`. A cache trained on one app works for the other app (+0 / +46 ms).
- Relocation: the same jars copied to another directory (`cp -a`) still use the cache. A jar whose mtime changed is rejected: `AOTMode=on` exits with "shared class paths mismatch".
- In auto mode, a stale cache prints 521 bytes of `[warning][aot]`/`[error][aot]` lines into the terminal, and a missing cache prints 211 bytes. With `-Xlog:aot=off` it prints nothing and falls back to normal startup.
- One-step training prints about 6 KB after the restore. That text includes the child's "Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: -Djava.class.path=..."; `-Xlog:disable` does not stop it.
- Two-step:
  - `-XX:AOTMode=record -XX:AOTConfiguration=f` costs +1.4 s at exit and prints one line.
  - `-XX:AOTMode=create` runs offline: 1357 ms, 37.2 MB.
  - The resulting cache gives first frames of 476-564 ms (3 runs).
- How a launcher could ship the cache:
  - **(a) Package time:** possible only with a bundled runtime (jlink), because the cache needs the same JDK build. That this requirement holds is stated in the JDK documentation; I did not test it, because only one JDK 25 is installed here. The archive must keep the jar mtimes. Train in CI under a PTY, with one union cache for all apps (+37-40 MB, about the size of lib/).
  - **(b) First run:** use `-XX:AOTCache=$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tui4s/<hash of java -version + jar names/sizes/mtimes>.aot -Xlog:aot=off` when the file exists. Otherwise run once with record mode and start a detached `-XX:AOTMode=create` after exit, with its output going to /dev/null.
  - Never use `AOTMode=on` in a shipped launcher.
  - The flags probably go through native-packager's `bashScriptExtraDefines` (not tested).
- Side finding: jatatui's NativeLoader extracts the .so into a new `/tmp/jni-*` directory on every run and never deletes it. There are now 753 such directories of 918 KB each; 532 of them come from my runs (about 470 MB). I left them in place. `-Djava.library.path` with `libcrossterm.so` stops this (checked: no new directory).

recommendations: Set the probe value in SchedulerDefaults: add "kyo.scheduler.blockingMonitorMinIntervalNs" (one line, no Kyo class touched). Measured -100 ms (Counter) and -69 ms (Dashboard) with 12800000, the value the probe itself returns on Linux. For other platforms, 20000000 (equal to the tui4s blockingMonitorIntervalNs, and above the known 10 ms Linux and 15.6 ms Windows counters) is probably safe, but Kyo's semantics for it are not checked.

Start the app without the bash launcher, or at least add -no-version-check (Universal / javaOptions or application.ini): it is 64-108 ms slower than exec'ing java directly, and the version check alone is 14-29 ms.

Add a daemon prewarm thread to TuiApp that loads the crossterm JNI library and links the Tty isatty handle while Kyo starts. Measured -113 ms (Counter) and -77 ms (Dashboard). It makes no terminal change and writes no output. It needs a test that NativeAccessDenied and NativeLoadFailed are still reported: the main path then sees NoClassDefFoundError, and loadError walks its causes.

Offer the JDK 25 AOT cache as the main packaging lever. On its own it halves startup (521 and 588 ms). With the probe skip, the native prewarm, C1 and SerialGC, the first frame comes at 320 and 395 ms. Ship it with -Xlog:aot=off and AOTMode=auto, never AOTMode=on. Options: package-time training under a PTY, with one union cache in a jlink image that keeps mtimes, or a first-run two-step record/create in the background, keyed by the JDK version and the jar names, sizes and mtimes.
Ship libcrossterm.so outside the jar and set -Djava.library.path. Speed is inconclusive (-64 / +24 ms), but it stops a 918 KB /tmp/jni-* directory leaking on every run.

Exclude org.openjdk.jmh from the runtime classpath (excludeAll on kyo-kernel in core). kyo-kernel's POM puts jmh-core and its generators, and through them commons-math3, asm and jopt-simple, in compile scope: 3.0 MB that is never loaded. Report this upstream to Kyo.
If an AOT cache cannot be shipped, consider the list-driven class preloader thread: -306 ms and -319 ms. It needs a class list made at build time and goes stale when the code changes.
Consider -XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1 for TUI launchers (-117..-132 ms, -16..-42 MB RSS), but only after a steady-state check of CPU and frame latency under load on the Dashboard.
risks: The numbers come from one 4-vCPU Linux container with a warm page cache and load1 of about 2 during the runs. Cold start, macOS and Windows were not measured.
C1-only (TieredStopAtLevel=1): steady-state throughput and CPU use are not measured.

AOT cache: validity across JDK builds is not tested (only one JDK 25 build is installed). A changed jar mtime invalidates the cache (tested). In auto mode, a stale or missing cache prints errors into the terminal unless -Xlog:aot=off is set (tested). One-step training prints about 6 KB after the restore and delays exit by about 2.5 s. Record mode delays exit by 1.4 s and prints one line.

Probe skip: it changes how Kyo's BlockingMonitor gets its minimum scan interval. With 12.8 ms on Linux the value is the same as the probe gives. On platforms with coarser counters, a low value could make busy threads look blocked. Not tested.

Prewarm thread: a JNI load failure now happens first on the prewarm thread, and the main path gets NoClassDefFoundError. The error mapping by cause walk is not tested. The class-list preloader depends on a list from a training run, which goes stale.
The prewarm and best modes ran on a temporary build with perf marks, which do nothing without -Dtui4s.perf. The other modes ran on the unmodified build from main.

The PTY runs left 532 directories /tmp/jni-* (about 470 MB) made by jatatui's NativeLoader. I did not delete them. Cleanup, if wanted: find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name 'jni-*' -newermt '2026-10-17 21:10' -exec rm -r {} +

The native image of the Counter works, and there was no hard blocker. Oracle GraalVM 25.0.4 (native-image 25.0.4) built a working Counter binary on the first try. I measured 15 runs per variant in a PTY at 100x30. The first frame comes at 101.5 ms median (range 99.2-107.1), and the shipped JVM launcher takes 1099.2 ms (1041.6-1190.0) in the same session. RSS (VmHWM) is 31.6 MB against 122.9 MB, and the process has 11 threads against 30. The native binary also beats the plain Java jatatui program (150.6 ms, 56.2 MB) and the best JVM AOT-cache setup (332.0 ms, 92.6 MB).

About 85 ms of the remaining 100 ms is Kyo's BlockingMonitor CPU-time probe, which is a sleep loop. With `-Dkyo.scheduler.blockingMonitorMinIntervalNs=12800000` the native first frame comes at 15.2-16.1 ms median (13.4-20.9). As a bonus I also built the Dashboard with `-Ob`: 104.5 ms (100.6-108.8) and 29.3 MB, against 1247.6 ms and 164.5 MB with the JVM launcher, and 18.8 ms with the probe skip.

The binary is 33.2 MB at -O2 with the full classpath, 31.5 MB with the unused jars removed, and 21.5 MB with -Os (7.9 MB gzip). For comparison, the JVM lib directory is 39.6 MB and also needs a JDK. A build takes 80-150 s on 4 vCPU, with a peak RSS of 1.8-2.75 GB. Terminal restore is correct on q, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM (exit 143), SIGINT (130) and SIGHUP (129): termios is the same as before the start, the app leaves the alternate screen and shows the cursor, nothing prints outside the UI, and a resize redraws the screen.

The minimal metadata is two entries: the crossterm .so resource glob and the isatty downcall `(int)int`. You also need the builder flag `-J--sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow`. Without it, a sun.misc.Unsafe warning prints into the terminal before the UI. These three items can ship in a jar as `META-INF/native-image/...` files. I tested this, and a plain `native-image --no-fallback` then works with no tui4s-specific flags.

I found two problems on the way. (1) If the isatty downcall is not registered, `Tty.isatty` lets `MissingForeignRegistrationError` through, because it is a LinkageError and `NonFatal` does not match it. The app then prints a stack trace and exits 1. (2) jatatui's NativeLoader leaks one `/tmp/jni-*` directory of 904 KB on every start, with the JVM launcher and with the native binary. Most of the steady-state frame cost is not paint. It is in four places that redo work or scale with the whole tree instead of with the change:
1. `Laid.without` filters the whole node map once for each changed kid.
2. `Paint.apply` compares every pair of paint roots.
3. Each `Mount.remount` scans the whole region map twice.
4. A relayout measures every sibling subtree again at each level, and on a size change it lays out the whole container again from scratch.

In realistic apps this gives O(n^2) cases:
- a ring-buffer log (`takeRight`), a delete at the top, or a sort;
- a list where every row reads one selection signal (also the 7GUIs "cells" task);
- O(n x depth) for every keystroke in an input that shares a container with a long list.

Two more costs: paint visits nodes outside the clip and wraps every text again, and the verify pass compares every Foreach item on every step.

    Laid(nodes -- gone.iterator.map(_.path), regionOwner -- gone.iterator.flatMap(_.owns))

- Complexity: O(S·h) instead of O(N·h); the ring log goes from O(I·N) to O(Σ S).
- Properties:
  - `without(l, p).nodes == spec.without(l, p).nodes` for all p, with l from generated UIs;
  - `regionOwner` equal on the live regions (the walk also drops stale owner entries that the filter keeps today);
  - I1 holds after random relayout sequences (no orphan nodes).

**F2, "drop paths under another path" (Q2, Q4).** S.
- Spec: `ps.filterNot(p => ps.exists(q => q != p && p.isUnder(q)))`.
- Law: p is covered iff one of its proper prefixes is in the set.
```scala
def tops(ps: Vector[Loc]): Vector[Loc] =
    val set = ps.toSet
    ps.distinct.filterNot(p => (0 until p.size).exists(i => set.contains(p.take(i))))
```
- Complexity: O(r·h²) hash lookups instead of O(r²·h). It keeps the input order, so the Runner's relayout order is unchanged. Also store `dirtyRegions` with a `Set` beside the Vector, so `markRegion` is O(1).
- Property: `tops == spec` on random path sets (duplicates, the empty path, deep chains).

**F3, paint cull (Q8).** S.
- Law I4: every write of a node's subtree lies in `n.rect ∩ clip` (fillBg, border, decorate and text all take `area`; kids take `content ∩ clip`). So if `n.rect ∩ clip` is empty, painting n is the identity.
```scala
case Some(n) if n.rect.intersect(clip).isEmpty => acc   // skip the subtree
// Txt: only the lines inside the clip
lines.slice((clip.y - n.rect.y).max(0), (clip.bottom - n.rect.y).min(n.rect.h))
```
- Complexity: O(visible nodes) instead of O(S).
- Oracle: the P5 property "same Buffer as the old painter".
- Note: P1 plans to delete `Rect.isEmpty` (Geometry.scala:25) as dead code. Keep it for this.

**F4, wrap as one fold that carries the width (Q7).** S.
- Laws: accumulating parameter `(done, curWords, curW)`; side condition width additivity, `textWidth(a+" "+b) == textWidth(a)+1+textWidth(b)` (a property test; fall back to a measure if it fails).
```scala
final case class Acc(done: Vector[String], cur: Vector[String], curW: Int) // cur.mkString(" ") at a line end
```
- `chunksByWidth` carries the width of `last` in the same way. Complexity: O(words + L), one Span per word.
- Then cache: `Kind.Txt(text, wrap, lines, atW)`, so paint does not wrap again (fusion by caching). Law: greedy line breaking is stable, `wrap(t, W) == wrap(t, W')` for `maxWidth(wrap(t, W)) ≤ W' ≤ W`. So reuse when `rect.w == atW`, or when it lies in that interval.
- Property: `wrap == wrapSpec` on generated text (wide characters, emoji, combining marks, long tokens, width 1).
- Also: compile the RawHtml regex once (Layout.scala:158).

**F5, measure once per constraint, by tupling (Q5, Q12).** M.
- Spec: today's `measureElement`, which is pure.
- Laws: strengthen the result: `measureElement` also returns the kids it measured and the width it used. `layoutChildren` reuses them when the constraint is equal (referential transparency).
```scala
final case class Kids(atW: Int, atH: Option[Int], items: Vector[Measured], regions: Vector[Loc], cols: Vector[Int])
final case class Measured(item: Item, props: Props, size: Size, kids: Maybe[Kids])
val kids = m.kids.filter(k => k.atW == node.content.w && k.atH == availHOf(node)).getOrElse(measureKids(node, env, root))
```
- `cols` are computed once (deletes the second `tableSize`), and `naturalOf` comes from `combine` of the measured kids.
- Complexity: O(N) for column or stretch trees, which is the common case: there the width at measure time equals the content width at place time. In rows that shrink or grow the kids, the widths differ and it measures again, as today. Never worse than today.
- A global memo table keyed by (ui eq, constraint) is rejected. Its result also depends on `env.content` and `env.focus` under the node: a non-canonical key and an unbounded cache (algorithms.md section 13). The Laid is the memo.

**F6, incremental relayout over the damaged subtree only (Q6, Q1, Q12).** M-L.
- Spec, the key property: after any sequence of events, the incremental Laid equals `LayoutSpec.layoutAll(root, env)`.
- Locality law: `measure(k)` reads env only at paths at or under k (content, focus), plus `screen.h`. Side conditions: a resize sets `full` (Runner.scala:233); focus moves are in the dirty set; bound values and carets change only paint.
```scala
final case class Dirty(changed: Set[Loc]):
    val touched = changed.flatMap(p => (0 to p.size).iterator.map(p.take))
// relayout(container): a clean kid keeps its natural, no measure
case Some(o) if propsUnchanged && !dirty.touched(it.path) && sameItem(o, it) && o.availW == inner && o.index == i =>
  Measured(it, o.props, o.natural, Absent)
// a kid that moved but kept its width and availH: translate its subtree, do not lay it out again
case Some(o) if same item, size, props && o.rect.w == r.w && availHOf(o) == availHOf(o.copy(rect = r)) =>
  translate(l, o.path, r.x - o.rect.x, r.y - o.rect.y)
```
- On a natural-size change, re-arrange the owner (integers only) and keep the container's subtree. Run `arrange` again for the container only when its box changed. Do not use `force` to lay it out from scratch.
- Replace the second full `layoutAll` on a focus change with `relayoutAll(old, new focus)`.
- Complexity:
  - a keystroke next to a big list: O(siblings) instead of O(list);
  - append to an N-line log: O(N) integer work instead of O(N·h) measures with Spans;
  - ring log: O(N) translates instead of O(N²).
- Properties:
  - P-L1: `layoutAll_new == LayoutSpec.layoutAll` on a generated `Gen[UI]` (shared with P5);
  - P-L2: Laid equality after random event sequences (Foreach append, prepend, delete-at, takeRight, reorder, Reactive switch, focus moves, bound writes);
  - P-L3, frame equivalence: the incremental damage painted over the old buffer gives the same buffer as a full frame. This catches missing damage.
- Rejected: a finger tree of prefix sums with relative coordinates, for O(log n) arrange. It is L, a novelty cost, and O(n) integer work at 100k items is cheap (unverified).

**F7, regions as a prefix-ordered map (Q3).** M.
- Law: under lexicographic `seqOrdering`, the keys that extend p form a contiguous interval starting at p.
```scala
given Ordering[Loc] = Ordering.Implicits.seqOrdering[Vector, String]
def under(rs: SortedMap[Loc, RegionState], p: Loc) = rs.iteratorFrom(p).dropWhile(_._1 == p).takeWhile(_._1.isUnder(p))
```
- `remount` takes `under(...)`, and `gcComps` only touches what this remount made stale (`comps -- staleKeys`, `pending -- staleDropped`).
- Complexity: O(S + log R) instead of O(R) per remount, so k messages cost O(Σ S) instead of O(k·R). Lookups become O(log R).
- Property: random mount and remount sequences give the same World (regions, comps, pending) as today's code, compared with fiber identity left out.

**F8, verify and reconcile (Q9, Q1).** S.
- Allocation-free compare: `items.sizeCompare(cur.size) == 0 && items.iterator.map(_.value).sameElements(cur.iterator)`, plus a fast path `cur eq lastChunk` (law: eq ⇒ ==). The fast path helps a direct `SignalRef[Chunk]`; a derived signal makes a new Chunk on every `current`.
- Structural sharing in `reconcile` when only the index moved: render, and keep the old UI value if `ui == o.ui`. Law: return the original node when nothing changes (Okasaki p. 25). kyo-ui nodes are case classes, so equality is structural and closures compare by reference. This makes the result unobservable.
- Property: `reconcile == spec` on the item values, and UI identity is kept whenever the values are equal.

**F9, diff.**
- (a) S, kernel: build disjoint row spans (union of the x-intervals per row), so each cell is compared once: O(d_union) instead of O(Σ d_i). Law: the diff is a function of the set of cells. Oracle: P5 properties (c) and (d).
- (b) M, measure first: op-level elision.
  - Mechanism: replace the triple Clear(old), Clear(new), Paint(path) with `Damage.Replace(path, old, bg)`, and keep `PaintMemo: Map[Loc, (Rect, Rect, Chunk[Op])]`. Skip a Replace when its rect and clip are unchanged and its ops equal the last ops.
  - Laws: writing the same ops twice is idempotent; I3, the subtrees of non-nested roots write disjoint cells; and no Clear of this frame meets the rect.
  - Value: the frames with `repaired > 0 && flushed == 0` cost O(ops) instead of O(cells).
